subject.title: Embedded agent: auto-rotate (or persist a marker) on context-overflow give_up instead of wedging the session until manual /reset

question: Should exhausted embedded-agent context-overflow recovery persist a durable blocked-overflow state, auto-rotate and replay the pending turn once, or keep manual recovery with better visibility?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally preserve the session mapping and surface manual recovery, while the issue asks to change core session recovery and durable state semantics for autonomous agents.

options.title: Persist blocked state first
options.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked marker plus operator-visible recovery affordance without silently replaying a turn on a new session.

options.title: Guarded one-shot rotation
options.body: Rotate and replay once only after compaction and truncation are exhausted, with replay-safety gates and a per-session loop cap.

options.title: Keep manual recovery
options.body: Keep the documented `/reset` or `/new` contract and improve only visibility, diagnostics, or docs.

recommendation.title: Persist blocked state first
recommendation.body: Add a durable overflow-blocked marker plus operator-visible recovery affordance without silently replaying a turn on a new session.

likelyOwner.reason: Session-store, session-management docs, and recovery policy history make this the strongest available routing candidate for the product contract choice.
